# Keep tooltips within screen bounds

## Problem statement

Tooltips are rendered at a fixed offset from the hover point without any viewport-bounds checking. When a hovered element sits near the right or bottom edge of the window, the tooltip overflows the viewport; in the DOM-rendered mode this extends the document's scrollable area, so the page "resizes to make space" (scrollbars appear / layout shifts). The tooltip must always be positioned so that it is fully visible and never alters the document layout.

## Users

- **Players** hovering cards, HUD elements, and buttons in Main Street, Lost Cities, Sushi Go, and the Gym tooltip/Gym-card-index demos.
- **Engine consumers (game developers)** who rely on the shared `TooltipManager` (DOM and Phaser modes) so they do not have to re-implement bounds handling per game.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I hover a card near the right edge of the screen, the tooltip appears fully on-screen instead of being clipped or pushing the page wider.
- As a player, showing a tooltip never causes the game canvas or page to jump/resize.
- As a game developer, when I supply a `phaserRender` callback I can clamp my tooltip into the game canvas with a shared helper rather than copying clamp maths between games.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DOM-mode clamping:** For a hover point near each of the four viewport edges, the DOM tooltip's rendered bounding rectangle is fully inside the browser viewport (`left >= 0`, `top >= 0`, `right <= window.innerWidth`, `bottom <= window.innerHeight`), with a small margin. Verified by a browser (`*.browser.test.ts`) test in `tests/ui/`.
2. **No document resize:** Showing (and hiding) a DOM tooltip does not change the document scroll size — no horizontal/vertical scrollbar is introduced (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` before and after `show()`). Verified by a browser test.
3. **Phaser-mode clamping:** The shared Phaser render callbacks keep their tooltip containers inside the game canvas bounds (`0..GAME_W` × `0..GAME_H`) at all four edges. Gym's callback (currently unclamped) is brought in line with the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, ideally via a shared, unit-tested helper. Verified by unit tests (helper) plus the existing scene/browser tests.
4. **No regression to existing positioning:** Existing world→screen coordinate mapping (canvas scale, canvas offset, camera scroll) and the settings `showTooltips` toggle behaviour are preserved; the existing `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` / `TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` expectations are updated rather than weakened.
5. **Validation and documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (tooltip component section) and any relevant Gym help text. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Must not regress reduced-motion, `pointer-events: none`, or the maximum `z-index` behaviour of the DOM tooltip.
- Must remain safe in non-DOM environments (`document`/`window` undefined) and when the canvas bounding rect cannot be read — fall back to hiding, as today.
- Clamping must be cheap (measure once per `show()`, no per-frame layout thrash, no resize listeners).
- The DOM tooltip node must not contribute to the document's scrollable overflow area.
- Use UK English in comments and docs; escape only backticks in worklog content.
- Existing tests that assert `div.style.position === 'absolute'` will need updating if the positioning strategy changes (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManager`. DOM mode computes `screenX`/`screenY` from the canvas rect, camera scroll, and scale, then sets `left`/`top` = point + `(10, 10)` offset with **no bounds check**. The node is `position: absolute`, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 2147483647`, `max-width: 320px`, appended to `document.body`. Phaser mode delegates layout entirely to the caller's `phaserRender` callback.
- Consumers in DOM mode: Main Street (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` constructs it; `MainStreetRendererStreet/Hud/Market/Layout.ts` call `show`), `GymTooltipScene` DOM half, `GymCardIndexScene`.
- Consumers in Phaser mode: `LostCitiesScene.ts` (`createTooltipManager`) and `SushiGoScene.ts` — both already clamp with `Phaser.Math.Clamp(..., 4, GAME_W - boxW - 4)` etc. `GymTooltipScene`'s Phaser callback does **not** clamp.
- Tests: `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` (unit), `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` (browser, asserts `position === 'absolute'`), `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` (SLL anchors only), plus Main Street tooltip content tests.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents `TooltipManager`; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` maps the tooltip scenes.

## Desired change

- Add viewport-bounds clamping to the shared DOM tooltip renderer in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`:
  - Position the node relative to the viewport so it cannot extend the document scroll area (e.g. `position: fixed`).
  - Measure the node after setting content, then flip it above/left of the hover point when there is not enough room below/right, and clamp to the viewport as a final guard, keeping a small margin.
  - Keep the existing world→screen conversion (canvas rect + camera scroll + scale).
- Extract a reusable bounds-clamping helper for in-canvas (Phaser) tooltips, mirroring the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, and use it in `GymTooltipScene` (and optionally migrate Lost Cities / Sushi Go to the shared helper with no behaviour change).
- Add unit tests for the clamp maths (all four edges, both axes, oversized tooltip) and browser tests proving the tooltip stays in the viewport and does not change document scroll size.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and Gym help text if the scene behaviour/description changes).
- **Test-first:** author the clamp-helper unit tests and the browser edge/document-scroll tests before wiring the DOM renderer and the Gym callback, so the new behaviour is specified by failing tests first.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — Add DOM-mode viewport clamping / anti-resize positioning; export a reusable Phaser-mode clamp helper.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — Apply the clamp helper in the `phaserRender` callback (currently unclamped).
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — Unit tests for clamp maths via the DOM mock and helper.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — Edge-position + document-scroll-size assertions; update the `position` selector assumption.
- `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` — Extend with Gym Phaser-mode in-bounds assertions (if the scene callback is changed).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the bounds guarantee for both tooltip modes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the correct, complete interpretation of the title is "no tooltip (in either DOM or Phaser mode) may render outside its visible bounds", not just the DOM overlay. The DOM mode is the cause of the reported page-resize; Phaser mode only clips. Recommended and assumed.
- **Assumption:** clamping (shift/flip to stay visible) is preferred over truncating content or shrinking the tooltip. Documented assumption; trivially revisitable.
- **Risk:** switching the DOM node to `position: fixed` invalidates the existing browser test's `position === 'absolute'` selector — update the selector to target the tooltip by its stable attributes (`pointer-events: none` + `z-index`) rather than `position`.
- **Risk:** measuring the node to clamp requires it to be laid out; setting `display: block` before measuring may cause a one-frame flash. Mitigate by measuring immediately after content is set and before paint (single synchronous reflow), or measure with `visibility: hidden` then reveal.
- **Risk:** `window`/`document` may be undefined in unit tests/SSR — guard clamping behind the existing `document` checks and fall back to the unclamped path (or hide) when dimensions are unavailable.
- **Risk:** double clamping when a game's `phaserRender` already clamps — the helper must be opt-in and not re-apply automatically to caller-managed containers.
- **Risk:** oversized tooltips (taller/wider than the viewport) cannot fit; clamp to the margin and accept partial visibility, documenting the behaviour.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tooltip content wrapping/truncation, touch/long-press tooltips, and tooltip theming are out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Related work

- **CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7** – Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover (completed) — introduced the shared `TooltipManager` this bug affects.
- **CG-0MODIX70W002JXQN** – `feat(ui): add TooltipManager` / `fix(ui): DOM-positioned tooltip displays above cards` — prior DOM coordinate-mapping work in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`.
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed) — SLL precedent for declarative positioning.
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed) — SLL layout system; relevant if bounds handling is expressed via SLL zones.
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed) — Main Street tooltip content fix, no overlap with positioning.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed)
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ake, bounds, displayed, ensure, keep (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+10 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+7 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q:** Are there open questions requiring producer input? — **A:** No. The seed context ("Sometimes when a tooltip is displayed it would render outside the screen bounds. This results in the screen resizing to make space. We need to ensure that the tooltip is positioned such that it stays within screen bounds.") plus repository research was sufficient to draft a clear, testable brief. No interview round was required. Source: seed context supplied with the intake invocation + repo inspection.

**Prior related answers:** none.

**Research summary:** Inspected `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` (DOM node is `position: absolute` on `document.body` with no bounds check — the resize cause; Phaser mode delegates to `phaserRender`), the four in-repo consumers (Main Street, Gym DOM, Gym Phaser, Lost Cities, Sushi Go), and the existing tests/docs. Lost Cities and Sushi Go already clamp inside the canvas with `Phaser.Math.Clamp`; Gym and the DOM renderer do not. No existing shared clamp helper exists. Related completed tooltip work items were found via `wl search` (see automated report).

# Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (WL-0MTH6B20C002ZOM2) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

The Pawn Shop business card (`biz-pawnshop`, Main Street game, `Tableau-Card-Engine`) is currently **increasing** the player's reputation by +5 per turn and costs 300 coins to purchase — both incorrect per design intent. A pawn shop should be a low-reputation, budget-friendly establishment: it should **reduce** reputation by 0.1 per turn and be cheaper to acquire (200 coins at the ×100 scale, i.e. 2.00 in game terms).

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I expect placing a Pawn Shop on my street to slightly harm my reputation each turn (`-0.1`), not boost it, so that reputation decisions involve meaningful trade-offs.
- **As a player**, I expect the Pawn Shop to remain an accessible budget business (cheaper than the 300-coin tier-2 group) despite its per-turn reputation penalty.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect CSV card data and tests to stay internally consistent (numeric columns valid; ongoing-cost convention preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Negative reputation per turn.** `biz-pawnshop.reputationPerTurn` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` changes from `5` to `-10` (the ×100 integer-economy representation of the design value −0.1; see CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); placing the Pawn Shop on the street grid accrues a **negative** reputation delta (−10) during the income phase (`applyIncome`), never a positive one.
2. **Reduced purchase cost.** `biz-pawnshop.cost` in the CSV changes from `300` to `200`; the market purchase price for the Pawn Shop is 200 (2.00 at the ×100 display convention).
3. **Synergy opt-out unchanged.** The Pawn Shop still provides and receives **zero** synergy bonuses (`synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, no adjacency synergy) — unchanged behaviour (existing tests in `adjacency.test.ts` / `MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` still pass).
4. **Test coverage.** Add or extend automated tests asserting (a) the Pawn Shop's negative per-turn reputation and (b) its updated cost of 200; the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (card tooltips/descriptions generated from CSV, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` and any README/wikis as applicable, including code comments). Note: `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- CSV numeric columns are validated by `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (`parseFloat`); `-0.1` is a valid numeric value.
- Costs use the ×100 integer convention (200 = 2.00 coins); `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw at income time (no ×100) — confirm via tests during implementation.
- **Do not** regenerate costs via the balance-cards curve tool (`src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts`): it would reassign tier bands. Its Pawn Shop special case (cost −2) applies only when `baseIncome === 0`, which is not our case — no algorithm change needed.
- Ongoing-cost convention (documented in `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts`) is `max(25, cost / 4)`. **Assumption (producer to confirm):** if `cost` becomes 200, `ongoingCost` follows the convention to 50 (currently 75). The producer's clarification specified only the purchase cost; do not change `ongoingCost` unless confirmed.

## Existing state

Current `biz-pawnshop` row in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`:

```
business,biz-pawnshop,Pawn Shop,300,230,Commerce,...,1,5,0,0,Trades second-hand goods. Does not provide or receive synergy bonuses.,2,...,75,...
```

- `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 230`, `reputationPerTurn = 5`, `synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`, `tier = 2`, `ongoingCost = 75`.
- The Pawn Shop currently **adds** 5 reputation per turn (raw ledger units) and costs 3.00 coins (×100: 300).
- All six tier-2 businesses share `cost 300 / income 230 / rep 5 / ongoingCost 75`; changing only the Pawn Shop is a deliberate divergence.

## Desired change

| Field | Current | Desired |
|---|---|---|
| `reputationPerTurn` | `5` | `-10` (×100 integer economy; reduces reputation by 0.1/turn in design terms) |
| `cost` | `300` | `200` (2.00 at ×100) |
| `ongoingCost` | `75` | `50` — **assumption**, follows `cost/4` convention; pending confirmation |
| `synergyCoinBonus` / `synergyRepBonus` / `tier` / `baseIncome` | `0` / `0` / `2` / `230` | unchanged |

## Risks & assumptions

- **Ongoing-cost convention (assumption, unconfirmed).** Changing `cost` to 200 implies `ongoingCost = 50` per the documented `max(25, cost/4)` convention; the producer's clarification only covered the purchase cost. Implementer should confirm before touching `ongoingCost`; leaving it at 75 leaves a convention inconsistency (risk: low).
- **Unit conventions.** Costs are ×100 integers; `reputationPerTurn` is applied raw. If the game's ×100 scaling applies to reputation in the current branch, `-0.1` may need to be stored as `-10` — validate against the repo's existing tests before finalising the CSV value (risk: medium; mitigated by AC1's negative-delta assertion).
- **Do not regenerate balances.** Running the balance-cards tool would reassign the Pawn Shop's tier band and overwrite the manual cost; the change is a data-only edit plus tests.
- **Scope-creep guard.** The Pawn Shop's card *description* text could mention its reputation penalty, but that is an extra opportunity — record as a linked work item if desired, not part of this item's scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Pawn Shop row: `reputationPerTurn`, `cost` (and `ongoingCost` per assumption)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — template loading from CSV (read-only; verifies `-0.1` and `200` parse)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `applyIncome` reputation accrual loop (read-only; confirms negative deltas apply)
- `tests/main-street/…` — new/extended tests (e.g. alongside `business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` / `turn-cash-net.test.ts`) for negative rep/turn and cost 200
- `src/balance-cards/algorithm.ts` — no change expected (verify special case is unaffected)
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — update if the Pawn Shop row description changes

## Related work

- `WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02` — "End of game stats" (open; text-overlap match only, no dependency).
- `WL-0MSGTSPXK007POB1`, `WL-0MT1KJNHE0048HW3` — text-overlap matches from the automated report; not related.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — documents the Pawn Shop no-synergy special case.
- Existing Pawn Shop synergy opt-out tests: `tests/main-street/adjacency.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/same-type-synergy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetHandSynergy.test.ts` (all covered by AC3).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

1. **Q:** "The description says 'Reduce the cost of the pawn shop to 2' — which field should be changed? `cost` (purchase price, currently 300) → reduce to 2? `ongoingCost` (per-turn operating cost, currently 75) → reduce to 2? Or some other cost field? The reputation change (from +5 to −0.1 per turn) is clear."
   **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "Neither should be reduced to 2. This is from when costs were lower, now it should be 200."
   **Final accepted answer:** the **`cost`** field changes `300 → 200` (×100 scale; 2.00 in game terms). The original "to 2" wording was from an earlier lower-cost economy and is superseded.
   Research summary: inspected `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` (pawn shop row), `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (numeric validation), `MainStreetCards.ts` (template loading), `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (`applyIncome` reputation accrual), `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (ongoing-cost convention `max(25, cost/4)`), and `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md`.
---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSGTSPXK007POB1** – Herdr worklist: remove blank line and redundant filter bar; show filter in header (completed)
- **WL-0MT1KJNHE0048HW3** – snapd udev monitor goroutine hang - watchdog kills and restart loops (completed)
- **WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02** – End of game stats (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: cost, increase, pawn, reduce, reputation, shop, should, turn
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: cost, pawn, reduce, reputation, shop, should, turn
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — matched: cost, increase, pawn, reduce, reputation, shop, turn

---

# Card outlines and card positions move when a card is added to the hand

## Problem Statement

When a `HandView` is configured with a known capacity (`maxSlots`) and ghost
position outlines (`showPositionOutlines: true`), both the card row **and** the
outline row are laid out relative to the *current* card count. Adding a card
therefore re-centres the whole row: every existing card and every slot shifts
laterally, and it only stops moving once the hand reaches `maxSlots`. The user
observes "the left card becomes centred and the two to the right are pushed
right; then when another card is added they all move left one slot".

Slot positions should be derived from the hand's **capacity**, not its current
size, so an occupied slot stays put as cards are added and the row only
re-lays when a slot is added (capacity change).

## Users

- **Player (Main Street, Gym)** — builds a stable spatial memory of where each
  held card sits; cards appear in the next free slot instead of shuffling under
  the pointer. Also keeps the ghost capacity outline in the same place as the
  card that later fills it.
- **Developer** — relies on `HandView` for layout; no scene-level workaround or
  bespoke hand rendering should be required to get stable slots.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, when I buy a second business card into my (capacity
  3) hand, the first card stays exactly where it was and the new card appears to
  its right.
- As a Gym user, drawing a 6th card into the 7-slot hand does not move the
  first five cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With `maxSlots` set, the set of outline slot positions for a given capacity
   is **identical** for a hand of 0, 1, … `maxSlots` cards (measured: the
   `outlineRects[i].x` for every `i` is unchanged across `setCards` of each
   size).
2. Adding a card places it in the next empty slot to the right of the occupied
   run, and every already-placed card keeps its pre-add position (measured:
   for `addCard`, `sprite[i].x` before === after for all pre-existing `i`).
3. Occupied outline slots still sit at the exact card position and rotation
   (`rect.x/y/rotation === sprite.x/y/rotation`), and extra capacity slots still
   render below every card — the CG-0MT6ER7YY003G680 invariant is preserved.
4. Changing capacity (`setMaxSlots(n)`) re-lays the whole row and always yields
   exactly `n` slots; this is the only mutation that may move existing cards.
5. The empty-hand capacity row is unchanged from today's behaviour — `maxSlots`
   straight/arc slots centred on the hand centre — so an empty hand still shows
   the full capacity in the same place the cards will occupy.
6. Unit tests (`tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`) verify AC 1–5, including a
   regression test that asserts positions do **not** move across successive
   `addCard`/`setCards` calls up to capacity, and that `setMaxSlots` does
   re-layout.
7. Browser tests (`tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts`,
   `tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts`) assert slot/card position
   stability across a draw/add, not just alignment at a single hand size.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Hand capacity outlines), `AGENTS.md` if the
   documented behaviour changes, and any relevant Gym/docs entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the shared `HandView` (`src/ui/HandView.ts`), not as a
  scene-specific workaround, because both Main Street and the Gym use
  `maxSlots` + outlines.
- Preserve the existing empty-hand capacity row (centred on `centerX`): that
  row *is* the fixed slot template, so no visual change is expected for an
  empty hand.
- The fix must honour the existing layout options: `spacing`, `maxWidth`
  compression, `arcRadius`, `maxRotationDegrees`, `cardWidth`/`cardHeight`,
  `centerX`, and both `horizontal` and `vertical` `layoutDirection`.
- Cards fill the capacity slots left-to-right; the row is not re-anchored per
  card count.
- The layout must remain deterministic (same inputs → same positions).
- Vertical cascade already derives positions from `baseY + i * spacing`, so it
  is already card-count independent; the change must not regress it.
- Over-capacity hands (transiently `cards.length > maxSlots`) are best-effort:
  the first `maxSlots` slots stay fixed, outlines stay capped at `maxSlots`,
  and overflow cards continue to the right with the same step. Normal gameplay
  prevents this state.

## Existing State

- `src/ui/HandView.ts`:
  - `computeCardPositions()` (≈ line 1719) computes the card row with
    `layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })` → the row is
    centred on the **current** card count, so it moves as cards are added.
  - `_computeOutlineSlots()` (≈ line 1299) handles two branches: with no cards
    it lays out the full `maxSlots` row (the desired fixed template); with cards
    it ghosts `computeCardPositions()` and appends extras to the right of the
    last card, so the occupied slots inherit the moving card layout.
  - `_outlineCount()` returns `maxSlots` when defined, else `cards.length`.
  - `_updateOutlinePositions()` / `applyLayout()` reposition and rebuild
    outlines on every mutation.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — already provides the centred, optionally
  compressed row maths needed to build a capacity template; no change expected.
- Main Street wires `showPositionOutlines: true`, `maxSlots:
  state.maxHandSize`, `centerX: handCenterX`, and syncs capacity with
  `setMaxSlots()` (`MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, `MainStreetRendererLayout.ts`).
- Gym wires `showPositionOutlines: true`, `maxSlots: 7` in
  `GymHandPileScene.ts`.
- Existing tests assert alignment at a *single* hand size but never stability
  across adds: `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`,
  `tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts`.

## Desired Change

- Compute the slot template once from capacity: when `maxSlots` is defined,
  derive the `maxSlots` row positions (using the same `layoutCardPositions` /
  arc maths used today for the empty-hand outline row) and place the first
  `this.cards.length` cards into it.
- Reuse that same template in `_computeOutlineSlots()` so occupied slots ghost
  their card positions and extra slots continue the template to the right —
  producing one consistent capacity row for both cards and outlines at every
  hand size.
- Keep `showPositionOutlines` purely visual: capacity-driven layout is keyed on
  `maxSlots !== undefined`, so toggling outlines off does not move cards.
- Leave hands that do not declare `maxSlots` on the existing centred-on-count
  layout.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`: derive card/outline positions from the `maxSlots` capacity template instead of `cards.length`.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — Likely unchanged; reused to build the capacity row.
- `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` — Add stability/regression tests (AC 1–5).
- `tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts` — Assert slot/card stability across a draw.
- `tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts` — Assert stability across an added card; re-check click/drag/transfer paths that assume the hand centre.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Update "Hand capacity outlines" to document capacity-driven (stable) slot semantics.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — Help text only if the documented behaviour wording changes.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` / `MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — Verify no scene-level assumption about per-count centring; likely no code change.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT6ER7YY003G680** — "Show an outline of card positions in the hand"
  (completed): introduced `showPositionOutlines` / `maxSlots` and the layout
  code this bug corrects.
- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** — "Main Street: merge business hand + held event into
  one horizontal 3-card hand" (completed): established the 3-card hand and
  `handCenterX` anchoring.
- **CG-0MQSFGE540037N6S** / **CG-0MQRXO41D009DH26** — "Write Tests for Staff
  Cards & Hand Capacity" / "Implement Staff Cards & Hand Capacity System"
  (completed): runtime capacity changes that exercise `setMaxSlots`.
- **CG-0MS937FT9006273E** — "Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight renders over
  cards to the right" (completed): the depth-ordering pattern the outline
  depths build on.
- Automated `find-related` report (below) surfaced: CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7,
  CG-0MQ54PYAJ001XCUG, CG-0MLTFFGBH1CEPC7J (low signal for this layout bug).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (design):** The fixed slot row is the *same* centred capacity
  row currently rendered for an empty hand. Consequently a 1-card hand places
  that card in the **leftmost** capacity slot (left of the hand centre) rather
  than at the centre. This is the direct reading of "the position of the cards
  should not move unless a new slot is added", and it keeps the empty-hand
  appearance unchanged.
- **Assumption (scope):** Capacity-driven layout keys off `maxSlots !==
  undefined`, independent of whether outlines are currently visible, so
  toggling outlines never moves cards.
- **Assumption (right):** Cards fill capacity slots left-to-right; the row is
  never right- or centre-anchored per card count.
- **Risk:** Main Street's `handCenterX` anchoring and the hand→street transfer
  animation (`hiddenTransferSourceCardIds`) may assume a centred row for hit
  testing or source coordinates. Mitigation: run the Main Street browser suite
  and the drag/click/transfer flows; adjust only if a real regression appears.
- **Risk:** `maxWidth` compression means the step depends on `maxSlots`, so a
  capacity change can shift positions more than one slot. Acceptable — capacity
  change is an explicitly allowed re-layout.
- **Risk:** Over-capacity transient states. Mitigation: define best-effort
  behaviour above and unit-test it.
- **Scope creep guard:** Games without `maxSlots`, and any non-outline hand
  behaviour, must remain on the existing centred-on-count layout. A broader
  "slots everywhere" redesign (e.g. right-to-left hands, per-slot assignment)
  is out of scope and should be raised as a new work item if desired.

## Clarifying Questions & Answers (Appendix)

The seed context plus repository inspection answered the material design
questions; no operator/producer questions were required before drafting. The
resolutions are **agent assumptions** derived from the requirement (not
producer statements); each is labelled for confirmation during review:

- Q: Which layout should a capacity hand use? — **Assumption (agent):** the
  fixed centred capacity row already rendered for an empty hand, with cards
  filling it left-to-right. Evidence: `_computeOutlineSlots()` empty-hand
  branch already produces this row; the bug report only objects to the
  movement, implying the empty-hand row is acceptable. The only alternative
  (anchor slot 0 at the hand centre) would make the empty-hand outlines jump
  when the first card is drawn, so it does not satisfy "positions should not
  move".
- Q: Does the fix apply to the shared `HandView` or Main Street only? —
  **Assumption (agent):** shared `HandView`, keyed on `maxSlots`. Evidence:
  both `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` and `GymHandPileScene.ts` enable
  `maxSlots` + outlines and exhibit the same defect.
- Q: Should toggling outlines on/off move cards? — **Assumption (agent):** no;
  layout is keyed on capacity (`maxSlots`), not on `showPositionOutlines`.
- Q: What happens when a slot is added? — **Assumption (agent):** the row
  re-lays out (existing `setMaxSlots()` behaviour), which is the one case where
  movement is expected.
- **Producer confirmation requested (non-blocking):** the consequence of this
  design is that a 1-card hand shows its card in the **leftmost** capacity slot
  (off-centre) rather than centred. This is the only user-visible outcome that
  changes for existing scenes; it is logically required by "positions should
  not move unless a new slot is added".

### Related work items
- **CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7** – Implement Multi-Use Card Economy in Main Street (completed)
- **CG-0MQ54PYAJ001XCUG** – Sushi Go end-game overlay text not visible (completed)

# Task: Extract and scaffold the nine repos locally with commit-count evidence

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer I have nine local repos in the final F9 `src/`
layout, each verified to type-check and build, plus the per-repo retained commit
counts and the source `dev` SHA needed as publication evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `git filter-repo` is available (install via the remediation documented in
   `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` when absent); `scripts/extract-repos.sh`
   is executed for all nine targets from the current `dev` HEAD.
2. Extraction runs on clones only: the source monorepo's `git status` is clean
   and its `dev` SHA is unchanged after the run.
3. `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all --core-root <core checkout>
   --repos-dir <parent dir>` scaffolds all eight game repos (writes
   `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `main.ts`, `index.html`
   and `configs/game.json`) and each game repo records the engine as the `core`
   submodule pointing at
   `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`.
4. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` succeed for the extracted core repo,
   `tce-golf` and `tce-main-street`; `npm test -- --project unit` succeeds for
   `tce-golf` and `tce-main-street` against the extracted core checkout.
5. The retained commit count per repo (`git rev-list --count HEAD`) for all nine
   repos and the source `git rev-parse dev` SHA are captured for the parent's
   AC5 evidence.
6. `npx vitest run --project unit tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts
   tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` passes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Install `git filter-repo` and run `scripts/extract-repos.sh` with an
  `--out-dir` outside the monorepo (no writes into the checkout).
- Record the source `dev` SHA **before** extraction and the per-repo commit
  counts immediately after, so the numbers are tied to a known revision.
- Scaffold with `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all` and run the local
  type-check/build/unit gates for core, golf and main-street.
- Change no scripts unless a defect blocks the run; any required script fix is
  recorded as discovered work rather than folded in silently.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/extract-repos.sh` — the extraction driver under test.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — the per-game scaffold driver.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — the partition contract.
- `tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts` — layout/extraction unit suite.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — scaffold unit suite.

**Dependencies:**

None. The F9 `src/` layout is already final and merged on `dev`, so extraction
may proceed in parallel with C1/C2.

**Deliverables:**

- Nine extracted (eight scaffolded) local repos.
- Local build/unit verification evidence for core, golf and main-street.
- Per-repo commit counts and source `dev` SHA.

## Intake: open questions for the producer (OPEN QUESTION)

**Context gathered (repo/work-item search).** The title/description describe a *presentation* defect: when an Upcoming card changes coins or reputation, the coin/bubble graphics should travel to/from the **right** target and in the **right** direction — the **HUD totals** when the effect is *not* attached to a business, or the **business card** when it *is*. Two candidate surfaces exist in the codebase, and the current engine has no explicit "business attachment" for one-off incident deltas:

- **Phased income animation** (`MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts`, `animateIncomePhases` / `runIncomePhase`): phases `base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → collect`. The `upcoming` phase reads the per-slot `SlotPhaseBreakdown.upcomingDeltas`, which is currently a **documented placeholder that is always empty** (`MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, `income-phase-data.test.ts`). The `events` phase already flies coins to/from each business grid for active `income-multiplier` effects via `SlotEventDelta` (`eventDeltas`), sourced from `eventSourcePoint()` (the Upcoming panel effect line).
- **Incident-reveal animation** (`MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts`, `animateIncidentReveal` / `animateIncidentDeltaBubbles`): the Upcoming incident card flies to board centre, flips, and bubbles travel **HUD ↔ board-centre card** by sign (loss: HUD → card; gain: card → HUD), per `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` and CG-0MU41XVNV002N2D9. It has no notion of a target business card.

Related engine facts: one-off incident/event deltas (`resolveIncident` → `computeEventDeltas` → `resolveEvent`) are always applied to `state.resourceBank` (the HUD totals); `EventTarget` is `'All' | 'SpecificSynergy' | 'RandomBusiness'`. Duration effects (`income-multiplier` / `rep-multiplier`) are the only effects *attached to businesses*, surfaced per-slot as `eventDeltas`.

### Q1 — Which "Upcoming" presentation surface does this item cover?

- **A.** The end-of-turn **phased income animation** (`upcoming` / `reputation` / `events` phases) — where already-resolved Upcoming-card effects inflate/erode per-business income and reputation.
- **B.** The **incident-reveal animation** — the moment the Upcoming incident card resolves and applies its one-off coin/reputation delta (currently HUD ↔ card only).
- **C.** Both surfaces.
- **D.** Other (please describe).

**Recommended:** **B** — the title ("coins/reputation *from* Upcoming … flow … to/from the HUD totals **or the business card**") reads as a resolution-time delta whose target is either the HUD or a business, which is exactly the incident-reveal moment; the income-phase `upcoming` slot deltas are a separate, placeholder concept.

### Q2 — What makes an Upcoming-card effect "attached to a business"?

- **A.** A one-off incident whose `EventCard.target` is `SpecificSynergy` (matching businesses) or `RandomBusiness` — the delta is business-scoped, so the graphic should route via that business card.
- **B.** A duration incident (`income-multiplier` / `rep-multiplier` active effect) that modifies a business's per-turn income/reputation — i.e. the "Active Effects" lines already shown in the Upcoming panel.
- **C.** Both A and B.
- **D.** Other (please describe).

**Recommended:** **A** — the wording pairs a coin/reputation *change* with business attachment, which matches a resolution-time delta; duration effects are already animated through the income `events` phase (`eventDeltas`).

### Q3 — Is this presentational only, and which direction convention applies?

- **A.** Presentational only — the delta still credits/debits the HUD resource bank exactly as today; only the *graphic* routes via the affected business card. Direction follows the existing incident convention: **loss = resource → card**, **gain = card → resource**; reduced-motion and replay/headless keep the existing no-flight exemption.
- **B.** Mechanical — the delta should actually be applied to/consumed from the business card rather than the HUD bank (a gameplay change, not just VFX).
- **C.** Other (please describe).

**Recommended:** **A** — the description says the *graphics* should flow, implying a pure VFX change with no economy/state mutation.

> Once Q1–Q3 are answered, intake can be completed and effort/risk estimated. Assumption recorded pending answers: this is a `bug` (current flow target/direction is incorrect), priority `medium`.
